Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36252: ci, iwyu: skip subtrees in compilation database

01e3eca2d8ee755eed4488a44093759f0eddcb34 ci, iwyu: skip subtrees in compilation database (Ryan Ofsky)

Pull request description:

  **Problem:** The IWYU CI job analyzes `src/ipc/libmultiprocess/` even though its results are thrown away. Every run prints IWYU suggestions for 14 libmultiprocess files in the non-enforced pass, applies them, and then reverts them with the `git restore` from #36112. The suggestions also disagree with what libmultiprocess's own IWYU CI reports (it runs with `-Xiwyu --error` and passes), because the two jobs use different IWYU versions and mapping files. libmultiprocess is the only subtree in this situation; leveldb, crc32c, minisketch and secp256k1 are already excluded from `compile_commands.json` with `EXPORT_COMPILE_COMMANDS OFF`. #35361 reported this output and said IWYU shouldn't be running on subtrees.

  **Solution:** Filter `SHARED_EXCLUDED_SUBTREES` (from `test/lint/lint_ignore_dirs.py`) out of `compile_commands.json` at the start of the IWYU section of `ci/test/03_test_script.sh`, so subtree sources are neither analyzed nor edited. This is done in the CI script rather than in cmake so that only IWYU is affected: clang-tidy keeps running on libmultiprocess, and no list of subtree targets has to be maintained in `cmake/libmultiprocess.cmake` (that approach broke `-DBUILD_TESTS=OFF` in #35418 and was reverted in #35523). The change is three lines in `ci/test/03_test_script.sh`; the rest of the diff is comments.

  **Testing note:** You can confirm this works by checking the IWYU CI logs and confirming that output like `/home/runner/work/_temp/src/ipc/libmultiprocess/src/mp/gen.cpp should add these lines:` no longer appears.

Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36613: test: add getblockfilter test coverage for header-only blocks

64cf455b481d36182957bdcfcae7c411a7879897 test: add getblockfilter test coverage for header-only blocks (Aaron Leeb)

Pull request description:

  Add functional coverage for the `getblockfilter` error raised when a node has a known block header, but the block has never been connected.

  This gap in test coverage was identified by a coverage report generated while exploring BIP 157/158. The branch in `src/rpc/blockchain.cpp` was never executed in the measured tests:
  https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/64cf455b481d36182957bdcfcae7c411a7879897/src/rpc/blockchain.cpp#L3054-L3056

  The existing `getblockfilter` functional test checks unknown block hashes and filter retrieval for active and stale blocks, but doesn’t check a known header whose block has never been connected.

  This change submits only the block header of a newly mined block to a node using `submitheader` and verifies that in this expected state, `getblockfilter` returns error `-5` with `"Filter not found. Block was not connected to active chain."` This adds coverage for the RPC’s distinction between an unknown block and a known block for which no filter has been constructed.

  `rpc_getblockfilter.py` passes, and changing the error message makes the new assertion fail as expected.

Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36591: test: deduplicate PSBT unknown-field coverage in `rpc_psbt.py`

ef4310097bd651497a98a9d1bb59560a7055ae01 test: combine redundant PSBT unknown field merge cases into `test_combinepsbt_preserves_unknown_fields` (nebula-21)
40eba5eb20ba0041a6328ba3482fcc26ddbe0185 test: extract unknown fields passthrough to its own method (nebula-21)

Pull request description:

  I've tested some mutations related to test coverage for PSBT unknown field merging and discovered an inconsistency.
  <details>

Pull request description:

  Most supported operating systems ship with clang-19 (or later), so bump the minimum to that and allow new code to drop workarounds for previous clang bugs.

  (For this bump, only C++20 CTAD will become available.)

  This patch will only be released in version 33.x, next year (2027).

  For reference:

  * https://packages.debian.org/bookworm/clang-22
  * https://packages.ubuntu.com/noble/clang-20
  * CentOS-like 8/9/10 ship clang-21 via Stream
  * Free/Open/Net*BSD ship clang-19
  * OpenSuse Tumbleweed ships with https://software.opensuse.org/package/clang (clang22); leap:latest with clang-19
  * macOS 14: depends/release cross-builds are unaffected and use clang-19
  * macOS 14: Native builds use llvm-19-ish via XCode CLT 26.3 since https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36287
  * Windows: VS ships Clang 22

  On operating systems where the minimum Clang version is not shipped by default, the user would have to use GCC, or install Clang in a different way. For example:

  * https://packages.debian.org/bookworm/g++ (g++-12)
  * https://packages.ubuntu.com/jammy/g++-12
  * https://apt.llvm.org/, brew, nix, guix, or compile clang from source, ...

  `unsigned` is a 32-bit integer (even on 64-bit platforms). File sizes are generally measured in 64-bit integers and using 32-bit integers or architecture-dependent integers is brittle and confusing.

  So use u64 consistently for flatfile sizes in this refactor.

  Also, use `LARGE_INTEGER`'s `QuadPart` on Windows, which is recommended since C++11.

  Also, unit test VarInt overflow errors.

  The options for wallet funding RPCs have several issues:

  * snake_case aliases are accepted by the server, but unsupported by bitcoin-cli, not mentioned in the docs and rejected by the schema.

c000f6ef15e06856b9111ee433877a2b1bf31eb4 test: assert Murch-Zawy period boundaries (Sjors Provoost)

9f34ea1605bd0c8726cc69ecf5686cc6d3d0d125 test: rename REGTEST_RETARGET_PERIOD to HALVING_INTERVAL (Sjors Provoost)

Pull request description:

  This PR adds test coverage for what happens in the (extremely unlikely) event that the miner can't satisfy the constraints. This is inspired by the recently added timewarp-protection and Murch-Zawy rules (for the miner, not for consensus, see #30681 and #35949), but this is a pre-existing issue. It is not made worse by these rules.

  The test has an attacker mine 6 blocks, which set MTP at the victim's future-time limit. It calls `getblocktemplate` and the equivalent IPC method, which both fail. It then moves mock time one second forward, and demonstrates mining works again (and we don't drop the IPC connection).

  This (impractical) attack can be done at any height, be we illustrate it for blocks 142, 143 and 0 of a retarget period, to clarify that the timewarp-protection and Murch-Zawy rules do not matter.

  The test was added to `ipc_mining.py`, to avoid having to add IPC support to `mining_basic.py`. Mining coverage is currently split between various test files and not always mirrored between RPC and IPC. A followup could unify these, while still skipping the IPC side when that's not compiled.

  A few refactor commits to prepare:

  - fix incorrect name: `REGTEST_RETARGET_PERIOD` -> `HALVING_INTERVAL`
  - drop `REGTEST_` prefix from `REGTEST_N_BITS` and `REGTEST_TARGET` (consistent with `HALVING_INTERVAL`, `DIFFICULTY_ADJUSTMENT_INTERVAL` and `TIME_GENESIS_BLOCK`).
  - move `DIFFICULTY_ADJUSTMENT_INTERVAL` to the framework

  The last commit picks up a Murch-Zawy followup suggested in https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35949#discussion_r3944011135 and takes advantage of our refactor, but is otherwise unrelated.

4898199d8f97cad75cfd54a9caed3ffd3ce2948c build: suppress -Wc++23-lambda-attributes in warn_interface (Ryan Ofsky)
270f5dbe3ddac5191ec6b21ceb17c3dddb79b12f Squashed 'src/ipc/libmultiprocess/' changes from e8de5c7b68e..acded1aafae (Ryan Ofsky)

Pull request description:

  The changes can be verified by running `test/lint/git-subtree-check.sh src/ipc/libmultiprocess` as described in [developer notes](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/master/doc/developer-notes.md#subtrees) and [lint instructions](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/tree/master/test/lint#git-subtree-checksh).

  Changes since last subtree update (#35720):

  - Adds support for nonunix platforms, making API changes that are not backwards compatible ([#274](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/274)). Follow-ups add a `CurrentThread()` accessor matching compatibility code in [bitcoin/bitcoin#35084](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35084) ([#323](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/323)) and remove code for Cap'n Proto versions before 0.9 ([#331](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/331)).
  - Fixes a data race between IPC calls running on worker threads and disconnects, found by Antithesis ([#349](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/349)).
  - Fixes a use-after-free when a socket disconnects before `ConnectStream` connects, and leaks and hangs when a client `construct()` call throws ([#298](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/298)).
  - Fixes a race where file descriptors from `SpawnProcess` could leak into processes forked at the same time by other threads, by clearing `FD_CLOEXEC` in the child after forking ([#311](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/311)).
  - Makes `SpawnProcess` report `exec` failures back to the parent and throw, reaping the child ([#312](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/312)).
  - Adds support for `std::chrono::time_point` fields ([#303](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/303)) and for serializing lists of interface objects that need to be moved from ([#304](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/304)), both needed by [bitcoin/bitcoin#10102](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/10102).
  - Accepts container fields and parameters with any comparator, hash, and allocator types, like Bitcoin Core's `GCSFilter::ElementSet`, needed by [bitcoin/bitcoin#29409](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/29409) ([#379](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/379)).
  - Finds the `capnp` tool in vcpkg and Windows builds, needed by [bitcoin/bitcoin#32387](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/32387) ([#317](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/317)).
  - Adds a `destroy_connection` option to `ServeStream` and `ConnectStream`, lets `ServeStream` take ownership of the init object and return the new server and its connection, and adds an `EventLoop::incomingConnections()` accessor, simplifying test setup in both repositories and needed by [bitcoin/bitcoin#35932](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35932) ([#365](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/365)).
  - Replaces `EventLoop::post()` with `sync()` taking a `kj::FunctionParam`, avoiding a heap allocation per call ([#347](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/347)).
  - Names threads spawned by the event loop so they can be told apart in tools and logs ([#324](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/324)).
  - Fixes warnings that Bitcoin Core enables or plans to enable: adds `[[noreturn]]` attributes for `-Wmissing-noreturn` ([#339](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/339), for [bitcoin/bitcoin#35911](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35911)), and fixes `-Wunused` ([#362](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/362), for [bitcoin/bitcoin#36167](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36167)), `-Wunused-const-variable` and `-Wundef` ([#370](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/370)), and `-Wmissing-prototypes` ([#386](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/386), for [bitcoin/bitcoin#36743](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36743)) warnings.
  - Fails at compile time with a suggested workaround when Cap'n Proto misdetects exception support (`KJ_NO_EXCEPTIONS`), as happens on NetBSD ([#364](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/364)).
  - Build improvements: fixes stale generated code when the `mpgen` binary changes ([#316](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/316)), fixes `mpgen` link order for static Cap'n Proto builds ([#367](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/367)), links `mpgen` against `kj-async` instead of `capnp-rpc` ([#327](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/327)), shows Cap'n Proto `find_package` diagnostics ([#325](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/325)), installs `type-unordered-set.h` and `version.h` ([#350](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/350)), and shows include-what-you-use errors instead of failing silently ([#371](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/371)).
  - Test, CI, documentation, and minor code improvements: fix for a startup race in the example program ([#315](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/315)), new test for immediate client disconnects in `ListenConnections` ([#310](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/310)), `ReadList` return value check ([#338](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/338)), connect test race fix ([#343](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/343)) and cleanups ([#344](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/344)), `std::ranges::copy` follow-ups ([#307](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/307)), trailing whitespace removal ([#345](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/345)), Cap'n Proto version documentation fix ([#357](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/357)), clang-tidy updates ([#358](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/358), [#360](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/360), [#380](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/380), [#389](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/389)), new CI job testing newer cmake and Cap'n Proto versions ([#212](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/212), [#359](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/359)), CI coverage for the minimum supported g++ ([#330](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/330), [#366](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/366)), new CI warnings ([#332](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/332), [#341](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/341)), CI parallelism ([#334](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/334), [#356](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/356)), CI diagnostics ([#351](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/351), [#352](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/352)), Nix and LLVM updates ([#296](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/296), [#363](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/363)), NetBSD and OpenBSD CI fixes ([#321](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/321), [#340](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/340), [#381](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/381)), building Cap'n Proto with GCC in the 32-bit CI job to avoid an ABI mismatch ([#383](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/383)), and GitHub Actions updates ([#387](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/387)).

  The second commit suppresses the clang `-Wc++23-lambda-attributes` warning, which the new `[[noreturn]]` lambda attribute in `mp/proxy-types.h` triggers in C++20 builds. Since #31507 the Windows build uses clang-cl, so the same flag covers it.

  The third commit updates the minimum Cap'n Proto version in `doc/dependencies.md` to 0.9.2 (1.0 with Clang). This update raises libmultiprocess's own minimum from 0.7 to 0.9 (bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess#331), and libmultiprocess rejects 0.9.0 and 0.9.1 for CVE-2022-46149 and, with Clang 16 or newer, every version before 1.0.

Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36405: test: look for the wtxid in p2p_blocksonly

22535b460568be47e57aadfbe50d489becb77577 test: look for the wtxid in p2p_blocksonly (Ferdinando Ametrano)

Pull request description:

  In `blocks_relay_conn_tests`, the check that a transaction submitted over RPC is not announced to a block-relay-only peer looks for its txid among the peer's invs. The peer is a `P2PTxInvStore`, which negotiates wtxidrelay, so an announcement would carry the wtxid. The MiniWallet transaction has a witness, so its txid and wtxid differ, and the check passes whether or not the node announces it.

  This checks the wtxid instead. To see the difference, open that connection as `outbound-full-relay`: the old check still passes, the new one fails. It also adds an `outbound-full-relay` peer that must receive the wtxid announcement first, so the check cannot pass silently again.

  #35920 also edits `blocks_relay_conn_tests`; the two do not conflict.

  Found while porting these tests to https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-node-tests.

Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36142: net: validate Tor onion service replies and cached keys

0a53d12589c3116495a50a694006ce5ee220fb2d torcontrol: reject invalid service IDs (Lőrinc)
d0b447cf7f11d791622c919d2a0731bf33a7d33f torcontrol: validate returned and cached keys (Lőrinc)
3413d17028da5f5658af5637297013f8e396bafa torcontrol: discard replies missing a service ID (Lőrinc)
3601a1d1086b132f11db3b5e969d8fac9203decc test: characterize ADD_ONION reply handling (Lőrinc)
d63a8576d9beef910c54aabc388278897c16a41f refactor: prepare ADD_ONION validation (Lőrinc)

Pull request description:

  **Problem:** A node creates its onion service through Tor's control protocol and caches the returned `PrivateKey` value for reconnects.
  Tor reply parsing unescapes quoted values, so a control endpoint can return a value containing a line break or space.
  On reconnect, the node inserts that value unquoted into an `ADD_ONION` command.
  CRLF frames the remainder as a separate command, while a space adds further arguments.
  An unprivileged local process can exploit this by impersonating the default loopback endpoint while Tor is unavailable, seeding the cache, and releasing the port before Tor is available again.
  A compromised operator-configured endpoint can return the same malicious value.
  The reply handler also continues after receiving an invalid service ID, logging it and caching the key before attempting to advertise the invalid address.
  A later reply without a service ID can reuse an ID left by an earlier reply.

  **Fix:** This PR validates the returned service ID as a Tor v3 onion address before logging it, caching the key, or advertising the service.
  Each reply must provide its own service ID, and reply fields stay local until validation succeeds.
  Key validation accepts `NEW:ED25519-V3` or an `ED25519-V3` key whose Base64 payload decodes to 64 bytes.
  Returned keys are validated before adoption or caching, and cached keys are validated before reuse.
  A malformed cached key leaves the onion service unavailable until the operator removes the file and restarts the node. It cannot inject another command or argument.

commit.message:
fuzz: push a message to an actually connected node in connman target

Pushing a message to random_node, which is never part of connman's
m_nodes, meant that whatever data left in vSendMsg was never picked up,
and that actual peers in m_nodes mostly never had anything to send (the
queue of all nodes added with AddTestNode() was always empty, and the
v2 peers only ever had their handshake bytes to send).

Fix this by pushing messages to a peer chosen amongst connman's m_nodes
instead, to increase meaningful coverage of connman's operations.

  +            UninterruptibleSleep(333ms *m_nodes_disconnected.size());

  +            UninterruptibleSleep(33ms);

build: suppress -Wc++23-lambda-attributes in warn_interface

Lambda [[noreturn]] attributes before the parameter list are a C++23
extension intentionally used in C++20 builds (needed for compatibility
with -Wmissing-noreturn). Suppress the extension warning rather than
removing the attributes or working around them.

Uses the existing IF_CHECK_PASSED idiom so GCC, which silently ignores
unknown -Wno-* flags, is unaffected.

This change was written with Claude Sonnet 4.6.

98f9eb6afdfd2bb1cd2872bd7d2eb439ec2043a1 test: cover negative input in CheckTxInputs (KY-U)
133714d1695bc40277b213afd252c3e320cac73e test: cover cumulative input value range in CheckTxInputs (KY-U)
f8c6cd84e08043f206ca338d0ba7e4dc8bef5214 test: support multiple inputs in CheckTxInputs test helper (KY-U)

Pull request description:

  In `Consensus::CheckTxInputs`, the inputs are invalid if, for every input coin, either `coin.out.nValue` or `nValueIn` is out of range. However, the current `checktxinputs_invalid_transactions_test` only covers cases with one input, so the sum `nValueIn` is always equal to `coin.out.nValue`, leaving the [following mutant](https://mutanthub.space/mutants/275) alive.
  ```diff
  --- a/src/consensus/tx_verify.cpp
  +++ b/src/consensus/tx_verify.cpp
  @@ -189,7 +189,7 @@ bool Consensus::CheckTxInputs(const CTransaction& tx, TxValidationState& state,

           // Check for negative or overflow input values
           nValueIn += coin.out.nValue;
  -        if (!MoneyRange(coin.out.nValue) || !MoneyRange(nValueIn)) {
  +        if (!MoneyRange(coin.out.nValue) && !MoneyRange(nValueIn)) {
               return state.Invalid(TxValidationResult::TX_CONSENSUS, "bad-txns-inputvalues-outofrange");
           }
       }
  ```
  https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36686/commits/f8c6cd84e08043f206ca338d0ba7e4dc8bef5214 adds support for multiple inputs in the test helper.

  https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36686/commits/133714d1695bc40277b213afd252c3e320cac73e adds a test case with multiple valid inputs, whose sum exceed `MAX_MONEY`, while also having `nValueIn` != `coin.out.nValue`, killing the mutant.

  https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36686/commits/98f9eb6afdfd2bb1cd2872bd7d2eb439ec2043a1 adds a test for uncovered negative input case.

  Export the fields `replaces_txid` and `replaced_by_txid` from `wallet::CWalletTx` to `interfaces::WalletTx`.

  Export the fields to solve this.

  The QT5 GUI never used those.

Pull request description:

  `/rest/spenttxouts/<hash>` reads the undo file for every block above genesis. For a block that was stored but never connected (a side branch) or whose undo data was pruned, there is no undo position, so `OpenUndoFile()` fails and `ReadBlockUndo()` writes `OpenUndoFile failed for FlatFilePos(nFile=-1, nPos=0)` to debug.log with `LogError`.   This checks `CheckBlockDataAvailability()` for `BLOCK_HAVE_UNDO` before reading, so nothing is logged. Pruning clears `BLOCK_HAVE_UNDO`, so pruned blocks are covered too. The response is unchanged.

  The new check at the end of `interface_rest.py` requests a stale block and fails on master because of the logged error.

0771dd89d6eec31ea39f25b283aacbf2092c7c15 bench: add undo-data for BlockToJsonVerbosity3 (0xb10c)

Pull request description:

  blockToJSON only includes prevouts and fees when we have undo-data. The benchmarks did not have any undo-data, so `TxVerbosity::SHOW_DETAILS` and `TxVerbosity::SHOW_DETAILS_AND_PREVOUT` did exactly the same work.

  This adds the 136 KB of undo-data of block 413567 and uses it in the benchmarks.

  ```
  $ ./build/bin/bench_bitcoin --filter=BlockToJson.* -min-time=5000
  ```

  Before:

  |               ns/op |                op/s |    err% |     total | benchmark
  |--------------------:|--------------------:|--------:|----------:|:----------
  |       10,273,470.25 |               97.34 |    0.2% |      5.51 | `BlockToJsonVerboseWrite`
  |          104,973.68 |            9,526.20 |    0.1% |      5.51 | `BlockToJsonVerbosity1`
  |       17,071,753.65 |               58.58 |    0.1% |      5.52 | `BlockToJsonVerbosity2`
  |       17,256,754.10 |               57.95 |    0.1% |      5.51 | `BlockToJsonVerbosity3`

  Note that the `BlockToJsonVerbosity2` and `BlockToJsonVerbosity3` times were the same.

  After:

  |               ns/op |                op/s |    err% |     total | benchmark
  |--------------------:|--------------------:|--------:|----------:|:----------
  |       16,207,066.75 |               61.70 |    0.7% |      5.45 | `BlockToJsonVerboseWrite`
  |          109,119.99 |            9,164.22 |    0.4% |      5.59 | `BlockToJsonVerbosity1`
  |       17,907,169.45 |               55.84 |    0.1% |      5.49 | `BlockToJsonVerbosity2`
  |       34,274,126.50 |               29.18 |    0.1% |      5.30 | `BlockToJsonVerbosity3`

  - `BlockToJsonVerboseWrite`: slower as it now also writes the prevouts too
  - `BlockToJsonVerbosity1`: unchanged
  - `BlockToJsonVerbosity2`: slightly slower as we now read the undo-data and calculate the fee field
  - `BlockToJsonVerbosity3`: slower as it's using undo-data now

Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#31507: build: Use clang-cl to build on Windows natively

331902f1dda63b5b8e5e9296f9871c358bf5d2b3 doc: Rename `build-windows-msvc.md` to `build-windows-native.md` (Hennadii Stepanov)
fe2ffef6bc786e515b9fc99a4bf10792b45c6a91 doc: Add clang-cl release notes (Hennadii Stepanov)
4f1e6de6c44790c3abbaf83dfe09947610520e1e cmake: Drop support for the MSVC compiler (cl.exe) (Hennadii Stepanov)
720f381a264f8a136689bd50b29a78482e3b19f7 Couple `BSWAP_CONSTEXPR` definition to bswap implementation (Hennadii Stepanov)
4d7e07035dfd82730b8b1dcb17bee059e6102800 cmake: Adjust diagnostic flags for clang-cl (Hennadii Stepanov)
c4111989e47654db4325fbf3935228bd9385b392 cmake: Link to clang-cl builtins library on Windows (Hennadii Stepanov)
d2645f7ed486718d2af39cf5fc50f46bb8503be9 cmake: Always link `bitcoinqt` to `shlwapi` when building on Windows (Hennadii Stepanov)

Pull request description:

  Building on Windows using Clang instead of the MS compiler may be beneficial, considering the issues with the latter, as outlined in https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/31456:

  >    * non-optimized codegen: [build: remove need to test for endianness #29852 (comment)](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/29852#issuecomment-2049803970)
  >
  >    * compile failure: [MSVC 17.12.0 internal compiler error  #31303](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/31303)
  >
  >    * ~legal, but brittle stdlib: [util: Drop boost posix_time in ParseISO8601DateTime #31391 (comment)](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/31391#issuecomment-2510762011)~
  >
  >    * unspecified issue: [refactor: Check translatable format strings at compile-time #31061 (comment)](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/31061#issuecomment-2531244463)

  Additionally, MSVC does not [support](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cpp/assembler/inline/inline-assembler) inline assembly on the ARM and x64 processors.

  So this PR:
  1. Closes https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/31456 (and addresses https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/14118).
  2. Could be an alternative to https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/24773.
  3. Closes https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/36153.
  ---

  Additionally, clang-cl:
  1. Produces binaries with [better](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/secp256k1/pull/1681) performance. For example:

  | MSVC, block/s | clang-cl, block/s | benchmark |
  |--------------:|------------------:|:----------|
  |          7.40 |             11.52 | `ConnectBlockAllEcdsa`
  |          7.32 |             11.81 | `ConnectBlockAllSchnorr`
  |          7.38 |             11.45 | `ConnectBlockMixedEcdsaSchnorr`
  |         91.86 |            143.12 | `DeserializeAndCheckBlockTest`
  |        121.46 |            189.04 | `DeserializeBlockTest`

  2. Builds faster on the CI:
      - [MSVC](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/actions/runs/13792522864/job/38575846787) - 20m 35s
      - [clang-cl](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/actions/runs/13792522864/job/38575849680) - 12m 43s
